items.title: Russia says air defences shot down 170 Ukrainian drones overnight
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said air defences intercepted 170 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones overnight across several regions, including Bryansk, Belgorod, Kursk, Voronezh, Tula and Rostov, as well as Krasnodar, Crimea and the Azov and Black seas.

items.title: Russian court sentences woman to six and a half years over attempted Ukraine military donations
items.summary: A court in Russia's Oryol region sentenced a woman born in 2005 to six and a half years in prison for attempted treason, according to an account citing the FSB. Authorities said she tried four times to transfer money to Ukraine's armed forces; the verdict has not yet entered into legal force.

items.title: Residential building section collapses in Dymer near Kyiv
items.summary: A Russian military correspondent reported that a section of an apartment building collapsed in Dymer, northwest of Kyiv, and that rescuers were working at the scene. The account blamed Ukrainian air defences, but did not provide evidence establishing the cause or report casualty figures.

items.title: Report says industrial facility struck in Lozova, Kharkiv region
items.summary: A Russian military correspondent reported that an industrial enterprise in Lozova, Kharkiv region, was hit during overnight strikes. The report did not identify the facility or provide details of damage or casualties.

items.title: Authorities report major power outages after Ukrainian drone strikes in Donetsk region
items.summary: Authorities in Russian-controlled Donetsk said Ukrainian forces launched a large overnight attack on energy infrastructure, disrupting electricity supplies across a substantial part of the region. The scale of damage and restoration timeline were not specified.

items.title: Russia claims overnight strikes on Zaporizhzhia power facility and Odesa-area port
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its drones struck the 330 kV Pravoberezhna power facility in Zaporizhzhia and port infrastructure at Kiliya in Odesa region. It also claimed a cargo ship carrying dual-use supplies for Ukraine's military was hit northeast of Odesa; the ministry did not provide a damage assessment.

items.title: Russian frontline report claims advances near Serhiivka and Kupiansk
items.summary: A Russian frontline report claims troops entered Serhiivka on the Dobropillia axis and expanded positions near Shylivka, Bilozerke and Moskovka by Kupiansk. It also describes continuing fighting around Kostiantynivka, Vovchansk and the Sumy front; these are reported battlefield claims rather than confirmed changes in control.

items.title: Donetsk authorities say 279,000 customers lost power after overnight attack
items.summary: Authorities in Russian-controlled Donetsk said 279,000 electricity customers were left without power following an overnight attack they attributed to Ukrainian forces. Restoration work is underway, they said, providing a new estimate of the disruption's scale.

items.title: Russia claims 792 Ukrainian drones intercepted in 24 hours
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry claimed its air defences shot down 792 fixed-wing drones and four guided aerial bombs over the past day. It also said Russian forces destroyed a Neptune coastal missile launcher and struck energy and transport infrastructure; these are the ministry's operational claims.

items.title: Report says Ukraine's defence industry faces funding and production constraints
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal, as summarized in a Russian news report, says Ukrainian arms manufacturers face funding shortages, recruitment difficulties and risks associated with expanding factories. The report says Ukraine cannot match Russia's missile production volume.

items.title: Finnish defence official says Ukraine likely behind Baltic cargo ship attack
items.summary: Finnish Defence Forces communications director Colonel Huhtinen said Ukraine was the most likely party behind the attack on a Russian vessel in the Baltic Sea, according to remarks cited by Yle. He added that the reason for the strike was unknown.

items.title: Russia claims capture of Sosnovy Bor in Kharkiv region
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its Sever Group of Forces took control of Sosnovy Bor in Ukraine's Kharkiv region. The ministry presented the claimed capture as part of its continuing offensive operations; the reported change in control has not been independently established.

items.title: Five civilians reportedly wounded in Ukrainian drone raid on Krasnodar region
items.summary: Five civilians were injured during an overnight Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Krasnodar region, according to a report citing the regional emergency operations headquarters. The report said the wounded were receiving medical treatment but gave no further details about their conditions.

items.title: German commander warns Russia is expanding military capacity despite wartime losses
items.summary: German Brigadier General Christoph Huber, commander of Germany's 45th Armoured Brigade in Lithuania, told Bild that Russia is increasing troop numbers and arms production despite heavy losses in Ukraine. He described Russian industry as increasingly oriented toward military production.

items.title: Germany reportedly switches Lithuania exercise equipment transport to rail
items.summary: Germany reportedly changed plans to move military equipment for the Grand Eagle 26 exercise in Lithuania, opting for rail transport rather than road convoys through Poland. Reports citing Bild say the change followed NATO consultations amid concerns that a conspicuous armoured movement near Belarus could heighten tensions with Russia.

items.title: Lavrov criticizes German and British defence leaders over strikes on Russia
items.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov criticized statements by German and British defence leaders concerning Ukrainian strikes on Russian territory. The remarks followed a disagreement in which Germany's Boris Pistorius apologized for his wording in response to US Deputy Defense Secretary Elbridge Colby's criticism of deep strikes.

items.title: Ukrainian Orthodox Church representatives report attempted seizure at Kyiv monastery
items.summary: Representatives of the Ukrainian Orthodox Church reported an attempted takeover of the Church of St. Sergius of Radonezh within Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra. The people involved were not identified, amid ongoing disputes over religious property and control of the monastery complex.

items.title: Ukraine reportedly presses US to release European-funded Patriot missiles
items.summary: Ukraine is seeking the delivery of Patriot air-defence missiles funded by European partners under the PURL programme, according to a report. The account says shipments remain delayed because US authorization is still required despite European financing.

items.title: Russian naval corvette reportedly damaged by explosion at Libya's Benghazi port
items.summary: A Russian Navy corvette believed to be the Merkury reportedly caught fire after an explosion in Benghazi, Libya, while accompanying Russian cargo ships. Ukrainian involvement has been alleged, but the cause of the blast remains unclear and Moscow has not commented.

items.title: Four civilians reportedly injured in drone attacks on Russia's Belgorod region
items.summary: Four civilians were injured in Ukrainian drone strikes on Russia's Belgorod region, according to the regional operational headquarters. Further details on the locations and severity of injuries were not provided.

items.title: Donetsk health officials report poisoning after man picked up banknote
items.summary: Health authorities in Russian-controlled Donetsk said a man in Makiivka was hospitalized after picking up a 5,000-ruble banknote, and that his condition has stabilized. Local reports described dozens of other suspicious banknotes nearby, but the substance involved and responsibility for the incident have not been established.

items.title: Report says EU diplomat Kaja Kallas excluded from potential Russia talks
items.summary: Sources cited by El Pais reportedly said EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas was not considered a leading candidate to represent Europe in talks with Russia. They said the choice of participants would depend on the negotiating format, despite Kallas offering to coordinate discussions.

items.title: US reconnaissance aircraft reportedly flies near Kaliningrad from Lithuania
items.summary: A US Artemis II reconnaissance aircraft reportedly operated in Lithuanian airspace near Russia's Kaliningrad region on November 22 after departing from Romania. The account says such missions have become more frequent amid regional security tensions.

items.title: Czech prime minister rejects EU budget proposal, citing Ukraine funding
items.summary: Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis said the proposed EU budget was unacceptable to Prague, criticizing planned spending on EU institutions and financial support for Ukraine. His objections add to disputes over the bloc's future spending priorities.

items.title: Ukrainian drone maker reportedly extends FPV range with detachable batteries
items.summary: Ukrainian manufacturer Stellarion has reportedly tested detachable-battery modifications for its Deadliner R10 and R15 strike drones, increasing flight range by about 15% to 50 and 80 kilometres respectively. A Russian military analysis warned the technology could expand the threat to border areas and urged greater investment in counter-drone defences.

items.title: Report says bridge strikes have blocked traffic across Dnipro in Zaporizhzhia
items.summary: A Russian battlefield account says strikes on bridges in Zaporizhzhia have blocked vehicle traffic in both directions, including on the crossing toward the hydroelectric station. It also reports Ukrainian forces establishing pontoon crossings over the Dnipro; the extent and duration of the disruption were not specified.

items.title: Italy's Salvini demands apology over inclusion in Ukrainian online database
items.summary: Italian Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini reportedly demanded an apology after his name appeared on Ukraine's Myrotvorets website, warning that his League party would consider the dispute when reviewing future arms aid. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni criticized the listing, which was subsequently removed; Ukrainian diplomats said the website does not represent the government's official position.

items.title: AfD leader calls for refugee returns when protection grounds expire
items.summary: German AfD leader Tino Chrupalla said Ukrainians, Syrians and Afghans should return home once conditions no longer justify temporary protection. His proposal forms part of the party's push to tighten Germany's refugee policy, including for people displaced by the war in Ukraine.

items.title: Russian battlefield report claims expanded control in southern Kupiansk
items.summary: A Russian battlefield account says troops secured positions at the Kupiansk-Sortuvalnyi locomotive depot and expanded their area of control by about one kilometre in the city's southern Zaoskillya district. It also cites footage of Russian flags in Khrypuny and Aniskine, describing those settlements as previously captured.

items.title: Report describes prolonged water outages in parts of Kyiv after strikes
items.summary: A Russian military commentator says much of Kyiv's right bank has faced water interruptions for a third day following strikes on water utility infrastructure on Friday night, while service on the left bank was restored sooner. The account speculates that pumping equipment or its electrical supply was damaged but does not establish the precise cause.

items.title: IISS satellite analysis reportedly points to Russian Sarmat missile deployment preparations
items.summary: A report citing the International Institute for Strategic Studies says satellite imagery from June showed equipment and activity near a missile silo at Uzhur consistent with preparations to deploy the RS-28 Sarmat intercontinental ballistic missile. Analysts reportedly considered loading possible, but the imagery did not establish that the system was operational.

items.title: Russia claims strike on Dnipropetrovsk power substation and Black Sea cargo vessel
items.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces struck an electrical substation in Dnipropetrovsk region that supplied Ukraine's defence industry. It also claimed to have hit a vessel carrying dual-use cargo southwest of Mykolaiv in the Black Sea; damage details were not provided.

items.title: Zelensky cites 2,700 Russian drones launched against Ukraine in a week
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia launched roughly 2,700 drones, 1,460 guided aerial bombs and 165 missiles against Ukraine over the past week. He also criticized delays in delivering European-funded US Patriot interceptors, a concern he has raised previously.

items.title: European elections could slow Ukraine aid and EU enlargement, report warns
items.summary: A report citing The Guardian says upcoming elections in major European countries, including Spain, Italy, Poland and France, could complicate EU budget negotiations, enlargement plans and financial assistance for Ukraine. The analysis points to possible gains by nationalist right-wing parties as a source of political uncertainty.

items.title: Russian report alleges unmanned boat attack on corvette in Benghazi
items.summary: A Russian military analysis alleges that at least six unmanned boats attacked a Russian corvette believed to be Merkury in Libya's Benghazi port, with two reportedly reaching the ship. The account speculates about Ukrainian involvement but provides no established evidence identifying the attackers.

items.title: Eastern Libyan authorities confirm explosion aboard Russian warship near Benghazi
items.summary: Eastern Libya's government confirmed an explosion aboard a Russian warship at a port near Benghazi, with an unmanned-boat attack cited as a possible cause. Libyan military sources also reported intercepting another group of explosive boats approaching the city later on Sunday.

items.title: Power outages reported across parts of Dnipropetrovsk region after Russian strikes
items.summary: Parts of Dnipro, Samara and nearby districts reportedly lost electricity following Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, with some critical facilities also affected. Russia's Defence Ministry said it struck a 330 kV substation in the region that supported defence-industry operations.

items.title: Zelensky reportedly redirects missile funding from Flamingo to Neptune
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky is reportedly shifting funding from the Flamingo missile programme to Neptune missiles following stronger recent performance by the latter. The report did not specify the amounts or timing of the change.

items.title: Russian and Ukrainian accounts dispute control of villages in Sumy border region
items.summary: Ukrainian sources reportedly claimed advances into Novomykolaivka, Yunakivka, Oleksiivka, Yablunivka and Varachyne. A Russian battlefield account disputed several of those claims, saying Russian units repelled Ukrainian troops in multiple villages while describing Yunakivka as a contested gray zone.

items.title: Latvian firm develops drone-launched miniature anti-drone rockets
items.summary: Latvian company Rannon has reportedly developed 40 mm unguided air-to-air rockets for drone-mounted launchers, with a stated effective range of 300 metres. The report says tests against Russian drones are planned in Ukraine, but does not establish that the system has entered service.

items.title: Russian rescue vessel reportedly begins towing damaged Sparta II
items.summary: A Russian rescue ship has reportedly begun towing the Russian-owned Sparta II after an attack in the Gulf of Finland. Finnish military officials said Ukraine was the likely attacker and that the vessel subsequently drifted into Finnish waters, adding a recovery update to earlier reports of the incident.

items.title: Finnish Border Guard says towing of damaged Russian Sparta II is complete
items.summary: Finland's Border Guard said towing operations for the Russian vessel Sparta II have finished and the ship is now outside Finland's exclusive economic zone in the Gulf of Finland. The vessel, reportedly damaged in a suspected Ukrainian drone attack, is expected to be towed onward toward St. Petersburg.

items.title: Russian military correspondent reports drone strike on railway vehicle near Dnipro
items.summary: A Russian military correspondent reported that a Russian drone struck a railway maintenance vehicle near Dnipro on Sunday. The account did not specify the extent of the damage or whether anyone was injured.

items.title: Kushner outlines conditional US security guarantees for Ukraine
items.summary: Jared Kushner said President Trump could consider Article 5-like security guarantees for Ukraine as part of a wider post-war European security agreement. He said any commitment would require presidential approval, the US constitutional process and arrangements designed to make its activation highly unlikely.

items.title: Trump reportedly urges Europe to invest at home rather than fund Kyiv
items.summary: President Trump told European counterparts that billions of dollars would be better invested in their own economies than spent supporting Kyiv, according to an account attributed to Jared Kushner. The remarks highlight disagreement over the financing of Ukraine's wartime needs.

items.title: Reports claim Russian corvette sank and cargo ships were targeted near Benghazi
items.summary: A new report claims the Russian corvette Merkury sank after an unmanned-boat attack at Benghazi, while two Russian cargo ships, Anastasiia and Ascalon, were also reportedly targeted. The accounts add possible losses to the previously reported port attack, but do not establish the ships' final condition.

items.title: Russian strike reportedly sets train and platform ablaze at Lyubotyn station
items.summary: Reports from Kharkiv region say a Russian strike hit the railway station in Lyubotyn, setting a train and part of the platform on fire. Passengers were reportedly being evacuated as footage showed a large blaze.

items.title: Russian battlefield account claims advance near Herasymivka in Dnipropetrovsk region
items.summary: A Russian battlefield report says its forces expanded their area of control by up to 1.5 kilometres and took positions on the western bank of the Haichur River in Herasymivka. The account also describes Ukrainian shelling of Russian positions in the settlement.
